request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary for Case 1:

Patient Information:
Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 40 years
Gender: Male

Admission Information:
The patient was admitted to the hospital on [REDACTED] with symptoms of general malaise, arthralgia in his extremities, facial cyanosis, and fever (39°C). A medical history of post-traumatic splenectomy was reported.

Hospital Course:
Upon admission, empirical antibiotic therapy was started with ceftriaxone and vancomycin as the patient was diagnosed with secondary sepsis caused by meningitis from Streptococcus pneumoniae. Due to a severe hemodynamic instability, the patient was transferred to the ICU where they exhibited persistent hypotension and an inflammatory state with high levels of CRP and PCT.

The patient underwent continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) in hemodiafiltration mode for a total of 68 hours along with Cytosorb cartridge. During this treatment, a general improvement was observed in terms of the patient's hemodynamic and metabolic stability as well as reducing levels of PCT and CRP. The patient's norepinephrine demand decreased significantly throughout the treatment and the patient could be stopped from CRRT after 12 days.

Discharge Information:
After further treatment and observation, the patient was discharged on [REDACTED]. At the time of discharge, the patient was alert, collaborative, tracheotomized, and spontaneously breathing with a recovery of diuresis. The patient was advised to continue with follow-up appointments according to the recommended medical protocols.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Recommendations:
The patient was advised to follow up with medical appointments as per recommended medical protocols.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is pneumococcal sepsis, which falls under category **A40** (Streptococcal sepsis; A40.3 at full code level).

**Chapter letter: A.** The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is sepsis due to *Streptococcus pneumoniae*. This is an infectious disease, so it belongs in Chapter 1 (A00–B99). The patient's post-splenectomy (asplenic) status fits an overwhelming pneumococcal infection.

**Digits: 40.** A40 is the category for streptococcal sepsis, and pneumococcal sepsis is A40.3 within it.

**Why sepsis rather than the meningitis or other findings:**
- The source infection was meningitis, which on its own would code to G00 (bacterial meningitis).
- The Australian Coding Standard for sepsis sequences the sepsis code first when sepsis is present alongside a localised infection and meets the sepsis definition. Here it clearly did: severe haemodynamic instability, persistent hypotension needing norepinephrine, ICU care, and CRRT with Cytosorb.
- The meningitis, septic shock and asplenia would be additional diagnoses.
- Fever, cyanosis and arthralgia are presenting symptoms, not the principal diagnosis.

This follows from my reading of that standard; the actual diagnosis section of the summary was withheld, so I could not check it against the clinician's stated diagnosis.

CODE: A40
